title: Hadamard matrices of every order divisible by four
formal: For every positive integer \(n\), does there exist a \(4n\)-by-\(4n\) matrix \(H\) whose entries belong to \(\{-1,1\}\) and satisfy \(HH^{\mathsf T}=4nI_{4n}\)?
definitions: Matrix multiplication is over the real numbers. The superscript T means transpose, and \(I_m\) is the m-by-m identity matrix. The displayed equation says that different rows have dot product zero; each row has squared length 4n. Such a sign matrix is called a Hadamard matrix. The target is existence at every stated order, with no efficiency requirement on a construction.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof or refutation of the stated proposition, with all its quantifiers and hypotheses. Verification of finitely many parameter values does not establish the universal assertion.
why: Orthogonal sign patterns are basic objects in coding, signal design and combinatorial constructions.

context_blocks.text: The 2026 construction survey records the general existence conjecture while supplying new individual orders and a list of orders still missing. Solving finitely many missing orders does not prove existence for all multiples of four.
